steps.text: Mix sugar, cornstarch, and salt together in a medium heavy-bottomed saucepan.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking often, about 8 minutes. Once mixture comes to a boil, cook, whisking constantly, for 1 minute.
Remove saucepan from heat, and stir in butter and vanilla.

Spoon pudding evenly into 5 serving dishes. Let stand until slightly cooled, about 10 minutes. For best results, cover with plastic wrap pressed directly on pudding to prevent a skin forming and refrigerate until chilled and set, about 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Vanilla Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This homemade pudding is delicious and easy to make with milk, butter, sugar, cornstarch, and vanilla extract for an utterly delicious dessert.

video.description: This video shows you how to make a rich vanilla pudding on the stovetop. It’s quick and easy, and requires just a few simple ingredients: Milk, sugar, vanilla extract, and a hint of butter develop into a rich, delectable pudding.

review.reviewBody: Yummy! I love this recipe because it doesn't use eggs, which are, (to be perfectly honest!), a bit of a pain when making home-made puddings. TO AVOID LUMPS, do not follow the directions as written. Blend all dry ingredients in the pot you're going to cook the pudding in. Then slowly whisk in the milk until it's blended. THEN turn on the heat and start cooking! I added cinnamon and nutmeg, which is absolutely delicious, but makes the pudding not as "pretty" because it turns it a bit dark. We don't care...just like the flavor! I also added 2 cups of cooked brown rice, to turn it into rice pudding. If you like raisins in your rice pudding, just put 1/2 cup raisins in a 2-cup glass measure, add 1 cup water, and microwave 1 minute to "plump." Drain and add to the cooked pudding along with the rice. Raisins are an iron-rich fruit, and also add a lot of flavor!

This is a light and creamy pudding and delicious. The only thing I did differently was to put the sugar, constarch, and salt in my saucepan first and then slowly added cold soy milk - stirring constantly. When well blended I turned on the burner and cooked until thickened. No lumps! Another time I might add a little more vanilla.

I loved this pudding--and I can't believe how easy it was to make! As per another reviewer's suggestion, I whisked together the corn starch, sugar and salt in a pan before gradually adding in the milk. Then I cooked the pudding until thickened. Doing this made the pudding completely lump free! I also added a bit of vanilla bean paste for extra flavor (and to get to see those delicious little vanilla flecks in the pudding!). I also do recommend placing a piece of plastic wrap directly touching the surface of the pudding as it cools to help prevent a skin from forming. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

I did as suggested in a review, to put the sugar (less maybe 1/4c), cornstarch and salt in pan. Whisk well then turn on stove and while whisking slowly added original, unsweetened almond milk, whisking till it got to thickness. Yay...NO LUMPS! Same as recipe from there.

Quick note: please, please mix all the dry ingredients together before adding the milk. It will help avoid clumping and make the pudding thicken well. This is what I did and it turned out amazing! I also cut the sugar to 1/4 cup. It was the perfect sweetness for me.

Wonderful pudding recipe and it is so versatile. I can use this for a lemon, orange, coconut or many other flavors. I made some small adjustments and I got a nice firm pudding for a pie. I melted the butter with the milk during heating. Since I was making this for a pie filling I separated three eggs and added the yolks to the pudding saving the egg white for my meringue. Once I had added half the sugar mixture to the milk, I poured about a fourth a cup of the mixture over the egg yolks, mixed them together with a fork, then added the mixture back to the pudding. When I had added all the sugar mixture to the pudding, I turned down the heat and continued cooking until the mixture was very thick. I also added the Vanilla Extract before I did the extended cooking. I used a crushed Walnut shell for the crust. Not the best of pictures or the most beautiful pie, but it sure does taste good!!!
I am on Weight Watchers so I used fat free half and half and low fat milk. I also use purecane sugar free powered sugar 2T. I also tempered an egg yolk. Very smooth and yummy.

I used this recipe to make "cookies and cream pie", and added an extra Tbsp of corn starch so it would set up firmer. I poured the heated mixture into a graham cracker pie crust and added crushed Oreos. It takes longer to cool this way, but it's a fun and tasty desert.

Only used 1/3c. of sugar and 1 egg yolk. Dry ingredients into the pot with the egg yolk. Stir in milk before heating to prevent clumps. Stir till thickens. Add butter and 2tsp. of Vanilla. Top with cinnamon and a cookie for presentation.

This was very easy to make. Thanks to all of you who suggested adding the dry ingredients to cold milk. It worked perfectly! I did cut the sugar in half, It would have been way too sweet with a half cup of sugar.

Used 2tbsp of cornstarch, one egg yolk. I mixed the sugar, starch, salt first in pot. Then added cold milk (2.5cups) as suggested to prevent lumps (it worked). I stirred it constantly until it was thick. I might add less sugar next time. It’s pretty sweet.

Peanut butter pudding! Rather than Cocoa powder, I added two tablespoons of peanut butter powder into the dry ingredients. I also used 1tablespoon of GF flour along with two egg yokes instead of the cornstarch. It came out so creamy and tasty 😋. PS. I still added the vanilla, and followed the other directions. It was simple enough for a non cook like myself too.

Mine tasted salty and did not taste like vanilla. This was while it was straight out of the pan. I'll let it cool and see how it tastes. Hopefully it'll change is flavor and if not I'll be able to modify it with some powdered sugar and more vanilla. I'll update in a few hours.
It was terrible. When we removed from the Fridge it was like rubber. 3 tablespoons of cornflour, really. Someone hit the wrong keys I think. Anyway never again.

(Tried the 1/2 recipe)Lumpy, not smooth, and didn't thicken AT ALL with the original recipe. I used cold milk and followed the recipe exactly until I realized it wouldn't work. I mixed 1 tbsp of cornstarch with some water to make a slurry for it to finally thicken. Consistency was very gross---baby food and melted marshmallows that stuck to the pan---so I will NEVER try this again and you should consider my review (I would attach an image if I could).
I made it with a little extra sugar and vanilla. It was amazing!!!!
It came out smooth but very grainy. I was very disappointed. It was nothing like my mom used to make.
Love it, have made it several times. I use it to make banana pudding.
Follow all the instructions and it never set.

I made a couple of changes for some dietary restrictions. I sub Stevia or Monkfruit sweetener for sugar and almond milk for dairy. Because almond milk is thin, I added an extra tablespoon of cornstarch. The pudding came out great. So easy too. I will definitely be making it again.
